svg.title: Exoplanet transits: Jupiter and Earth crossing the Sun
svg.desc: Animated transit diagram. Jupiter, then Earth, crosses the Sun's disc as a distant observer would see it, drawn to scale, and each light curve is traced as the planet moves. Transit depth = (Rp/R*)² with R_sun = 695,700 km, R_Jupiter = 69,911 km, R_Earth = 6,371 km: Jupiter 0.1005² = 1.01%; Earth 0.00916² = 84 parts per million (0.0084%), about 120 times shallower, which is why the lower plot uses a zoomed axis. Central-transit durations T = (P/π)·asin((R* + Rp)/a): Jupiter 32.6 h, Earth 13.1 h. Curve shapes use exact circle-overlap geometry for a uniform disc (limb darkening would round the bottoms). This is how the Kepler and TESS missions found thousands of exoplanets.
